intro.h2: Kitchen remodeling in Durham, run by the founder
paragraphs: Ironwood Custom Remodels handles kitchen remodeling in Durham and nearby Triangle towns, from Hope Valley to Cary and Chapel Hill. Founder Ethan Randle moved into construction after his honorable discharge from the Marines in 2014, and homeowners work with him directly. Google reviewers point to his quick replies, detailed quotes and the time he spends explaining options.

Kitchens fill most of the portfolio. In Hope Valley, the crew moved structural walls and fitted new Marvin windows to open up a blue kitchen with Wolf and Sub-Zero appliances. In Hurdle Mills, they resurfaced hardwood floors first milled from trees on the property. Ironwood builds from your designer's plans or works with its own design partners.

services.h2: Kitchens, baths and the rest of the house

items.name: Kitchen remodeling
items.blurb: Projects range from new cabinets and countertops to a full layout change with walls moved. Recent kitchens added large islands, soft-close cabinetry, under-cabinet lighting and appliance packages from Wolf, Sub-Zero and SKS. The kitchens in Ironwood's case studies took 10 to 16 weeks from start to finish.

image.alt: Remodeled white shaker kitchen with a sage green island, white countertop, wood saddle stools, white cone pendants and a stainless French-door refrigerator

items.name: Bathroom remodeling
items.blurb: A bath can get new flooring, lighting, a tub, shower or vanity, or a new layout that uses the room better. Reviewers describe custom primary and guest baths and a downstairs full bath. Ironwood's 2026 spa bath guide covers curbless walk-in showers, soaking tubs and heated floors.

image.alt: Bathroom with sage green square wall tile, a frameless glass shower with a rain head, a tiled drop-in soaking tub and a gray vanity with a white top

items.name: Whole-home remodels and additions
items.blurb: When the floor plan is the problem, Ironwood reworks the layout so rooms flow better, or adds a bedroom, bath or living area that matches the house. One Google review describes an early-90s first floor where the dining room came out and the kitchen grew, with the family living at home.

image.alt: Open living room with a vaulted ceiling and arched window flowing into a remodeled sage green kitchen with a breakfast bar and wood-look floors

items.name: Basements, attics and specialty rooms
items.blurb: Unused rooms, basements and attics can become a home theater, gym, game room, wine cellar, office or extra living space. Ironwood has published 2026 Triangle guides on basement theaters, attic finishing and basement costs, so you can see the choices involved before your first visit.

image.alt: Large finished living space with wood-look plank floors, recessed lights, square columns and a white kitchenette with a granite island

items.title: A Marine veteran in charge
items.text: Ethan Randle served in the United States Marines and was honorably discharged in 2014. Google lists Ironwood as veteran-owned, and the company is licensed and insured.

items.title: Easy to reach
items.text: One client wrote that it was always easy to get a quick reply from Ethan. Another said he kept in touch just about every day, even on days he did not need to be on site.

items.title: Clear expectations up front
items.text: Reviewers say Ethan sets realistic expectations, listens to limits on timing and budget and provides a detailed quote. A home addition client wrote that he was on time and stayed within their budget request.

items.title: 4.9 stars from 40 reviews
items.text: Ironwood holds a 4.9 rating from 40 Google reviews. Ten reviews mention a professional team, eight a kitchen remodel and six a bathroom remodel, and several clients have hired Ethan more than once.

about.h2: Meet Ethan Randle, founder of Ironwood
about.text: Ethan Randle is the founder and CEO of Ironwood Custom Remodels. After his honorable discharge from the United States Marines in 2014, he joined an International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers apprenticeship. About a year in, he wanted work with a more direct effect on people's daily lives. He went to work full-time for a general contractor in Orange County, California, while attending night school for a degree in construction technology, and then started his own company. Today Ironwood focuses on kitchen, bath and whole-house makeovers in the Triangle and Triad. Clients call Ethan organized and thorough, and some have brought him back for a second or third project.

image.alt: Ethan Randle, founder of Ironwood Custom Remodels, in his United States Marine Corps dress blue uniform

process.h2: How an Ironwood remodel moves from first call to finished room

steps.title: Online form and phone consultation
steps.text: Send the short form, then talk by phone about the work you want, the finished space you picture and estimated pricing.

steps.title: In-person consultation
steps.text: A licensed team member meets you at home to walk the space and get a clear picture of your project and your goals.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: Layout and finishes are designed with Ironwood's design partners, or Ironwood builds from plans you already have, as the Hurdle Mills homeowners did.

steps.title: Project planning
steps.text: Scope, materials and order of work are set before construction begins, backed by a detailed quote so you know what you are paying for.

steps.title: Construction and move-in
steps.text: The crew builds while Ethan keeps you updated. The last of Ironwood's seven stages is simple: enjoy your new space.

service_area.h2: Serving Durham, Chapel Hill, Cary and the Triangle
service_area.text: Ironwood Custom Remodels is based in Durham and works across the Triangle and into the Triad. Its service list covers Durham, Chapel Hill, Carrboro, Hillsborough, Cary, Raleigh, Apex, Morrisville, Creedmoor, Burlington and Greensboro. Recent case studies come from Durham's historic Hope Valley neighborhood, the Cambridge neighborhood in Cary and a classic home in Hurdle Mills. Live close by but not on the list? Call (760) 642-6051 and ask.

faq.h2: Durham kitchen and bath remodeling questions

items.q: How much does a kitchen or bath remodel with Ironwood cost?
items.a: Ironwood has no set price list. Each project is priced on its own materials, labor and other factors, and the estimate is free. Your first phone consultation covers estimated pricing. For scale, Ironwood's 2026 guide puts spa-style primary bath packages in the Triangle at $45,000 to $150,000 or more.

items.q: How long does a kitchen remodel take?
items.a: It depends on scope. In Ironwood's own case studies, the Legacy Kitchen in Hurdle Mills took 10 to 12 weeks. The Blue Haven kitchen in Hope Valley, which included moving structural walls and new Marvin windows, and the Cambridge kitchen in Cary each took 12 to 16 weeks. Ask Ethan for your own timeline at the consultation.

items.q: Can we keep living at home during the remodel?
items.a: Families have. One Google review describes updating an entire early-90s first floor, removing the dining room and greatly expanding the kitchen while the owners lived in the home with their kids and dogs. Ironwood has also published a guide on phasing a whole-home renovation so you do not have to move out.

items.q: Can Ironwood build a design from my own kitchen designer?
items.a: Yes. The Hurdle Mills homeowners had already finished their design with The Kitchen Specialist and chose Ironwood to build it. On other kitchens, Ironwood partnered with Heather Holcombe Designs in Hope Valley and Chess Kitchen & Interiors in Cary. If you are starting from scratch, design is one of the seven stages of the process.

items.q: Are you licensed, and who handles the permits?
items.a: Ironwood Custom Remodels is a licensed and insured North Carolina contractor. Public permit records list the company as the contractor, for example on a Town of Cary permit issued in August 2026 for a primary bath and kitchen countertop remodel. Ask for the licence number when you book your free estimate.

final_cta.h2: Planning a kitchen or bath in Durham? Talk to Ethan's team
final_cta.text: Start with a phone consultation about the work, the finished space and estimated pricing, or send the short form for a free estimate.
